newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end up on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end up on short-covering.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended up on Thursday on short-covering for immediate profit with trading volume reduced as most investors stayed on the sidelines in light of ongoing market uncertainty, traders said.
The most active July 1997 contract ended at 22,910 yuan ($2,761) per tonne, rising 150 yuan. It opened at an intraday high of 22,960 yuan and hit a low of 22,800 yuan per tonne.
April rose 80 yuan to 23,150, May 80 to 23,000, June 170 to 22,970, August 160 to 22,910 and September 140 to 22,900 yuan.
Combined volume fell to 32,890 tonnes from 46,230 tonnes.
Copper opened higher and moved at high levels on short-covering for most of the session.

"Some short sellers offset their positions to take advantage of the current high values, but the thin volume indicated most investors took to the sidelines because they can't work out where the market is going," one trader said.
"Copper's gains today also supported the firmer spot prices," he added.
Shanghai spot copper is around 23,400 yuan per tonne.
Short-sellers hold most of the positions in the main contracts, traders said.
Some major institutions were trading thinner volumes, having already offset most of their positions, and had taken to the sidelines, they said.
Aluminium followed copper's trend. April rose 100 yuan per tonne to 15,450 yuan per tonne, May 150 to 15,600 and June 200 to 15,800 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 410 tonnes from 580 tonne.
